reply_text:
㊥ ("64% of Zai … mining the grammar of moves") Yes, and it fits the one gap the application still has: multi-opener turns, where no local rule links the reply to what it answers, and a grammar of moves is what scope-based linking would run on. Checking what exists (the transition tuner, the futon6 scopes, the Zai seats) before I shape the campaign.Checking whether the cold codex-72 seat has started my harness job, using a bounded until-loop rather than a chained sleep.㊥ ("64% of Zai to spend in 34 hours") Taken up as a mining campaign, and shaped so it feeds the one gap the inbox still has rather than producing a survey. Design, schema and the first packet are committed (2bbcdd4c); the harness job is running on codex-72 (`invoke-1791739453321-5677-80295469`, park `park-91af3f59`), after a slow cold start. Zai usage before anything runs: 36.0% of the month used, reset 2026-10-13 02:04Z, logged in the repo.

㊭ (what gets mined, and why each) Three things, all over the settled records that now carry acts.
1. **Answer incidences for multi-opener turns.** The kernel closes a port only through an explicit link or the sole-port rule, which reaches 112 of 575 openers. Zai labels which reply paragraphs answer which operator acts, many-to-many, each with a verbatim quote. That set is the test for any joint-coverage rule and the training set for a cheap linker, classical or Kimi.
2. **Moves beyond kinds.** One kind covers status check and commission, or plain approval and approval with amendment. An open vocabulary written `kind/move`, with counts, tells which distinctions the adjacency table should make.
3. **Scopes.** Constraints, "let's focus on X", mission naming, "back to Y": acts that open a region in which later moves are read, which is the futon6 analogy. A scope structure over sessions is what scope-based linking runs on.

㊟ (discipline) Offline, over records, as you proposed; not a live reader. A label without a verbatim quote is void, as in the memory judge. Output is a sidecar per record, never a change to the record. Pilot of 20 records on one Zai seat first, cost read from the usage meter before and after, then scale to the five idle Zai seats on the pilot's numbers. Measures fixed before scaling: precision of incidences against the 24 labelled rows and my census rows.

㊢ (also in flight) codex-70's reload and live recompute of the four record fields plus the session-end outbox. When that lands, claude-15's follower reads fields instead of running 象 code, and part 2 of the session-end work goes out.
